evidence: The agent checked release.sh:23 (`${VERSION_TAG#v}` then greps `## [X.Y.Z]`) against next-version.sh's `vX.Y.Z` output, and that confirms a reader of CONTRIBUTING.md alone would write `## [v0.1.1]` and block the release. The worked example in 6885fa4 labels both forms.
guidance_note: When one doc is restated in two others, diff the restatements against the canonical one clause by clause before opening the PR, especially transformations like stripping a prefix.

evidence: The original CLAUDE.md sentence ('bump CHANGELOG.md in the PR (`scripts/next-version.sh`), then run `./scripts/release.sh <version>`') never says the heading drops the v. The agent took the reviewer's second option, spelling it out inline, because delegating was ruled out by the maintainer.
guidance_note: Same move as F1: when compressing a procedure into a summary, check each value that changes form between steps survives the compression.

evidence: 6885fa4 rewrote CLAUDE.md into an explicit 'rename `## [Unreleased]` ... to the next version' procedure but dropped CONTRIBUTING.md's 'add a fresh empty `## [Unreleased]` above it' step, which the same commit kept in CONTRIBUTING.md. An agent following the new CLAUDE.md alone leaves no Unreleased section.
guidance_note: When a fix rewrites a summary to mirror the canonical procedure, copy every step of that procedure and check the result line by line against the source, not just the clause the finding named.

evidence: 6885fa4 introduced the heading example `## [0.2.0]` with no `- <date>`, while the same commit's CONTRIBUTING.md says `## [0.2.0] - <date>`. The reviewer concedes release.sh still passes, so this is a doc disagreement, not a breakage.
guidance_note: When writing a worked example of a format into one doc, copy the format literally from the canonical doc rather than retyping it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 'After merging a feature/fix PR' and 'One merged PR, one release' were both in the pre-review CLAUDE.md, and 6885fa4 did not change them. The opener already scopes the rule to feature/fix PRs, so only the tagline was loose, and narrowing it to 'One merged feature/fix PR' was proportionate.

After 8f2f40d the text reads 'After merging a feature/fix PR, cut a release ... One merged feature/fix PR, one release', so a docs/chore PR never triggers the imperative. The flag is a false positive: this re-raises F5, whose fix narrowed the scope on purpose; the fix did not introduce it.

The flag is a false positive: 8f2f40d touched only CLAUDE.md and next-version.sh is unchanged since round 0. The coverage gap is real; the reviewer's overflow and local-tag worries are padding. The agent's obstacle (copy the script into a temp `git init` repo with chosen tags) is a few lines, and the thread shows no follow-up ticket was actually filed, so the gap went untracked.
guidance_note: Ship a hermetic test with any new script that computes release identity: copy it into a temp git repo with a controlled tag set and assert each exit path.

narrative: This is a docs and release-script PR where the same procedure is restated in CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and RELEASING.md. The round-0 fix rewrote CLAUDE.md's summary but dropped the add-fresh-Unreleased step and the date suffix, and round 1 caught both. Round 1 also had a pre-existing tagline nit (F5), so the round would have happened anyway. Round 2 re-raised F5 (correctly rebutted) and asked for script tests, which the agent deferred without filing a ticket.
guidance_observations: Restating one procedure in three docs created most of this PR's findings; the agent fixed each restatement piecemeal rather than reducing the number of copies.
Deferring a valid test gap 'to a follow-up ticket' without filing the ticket leaves the gap untracked.

evidence: Workflow-level `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels the earlier run when the chore(release) run is created, before the job-level `if:` skips it, so the race is real. The agent abandoned the whole approach in issue comments ('would publish an unvalidated build'), which supersedes the thread; should_have records that redesign, since the enum has no no_response option.
guidance_note: When superseding a PR, carry its unaddressed review findings into the successor: this same cancel-in-progress hazard came back as #329/F8.

narrative: This was a one-round PR that skipped release-validate on release commits. The reviewer found a real cancel-in-progress race. The agent independently judged the approach wrong and closed the PR in favour of the build-once redesign (#329), without replying on the thread.
guidance_observations: The unanswered concurrency finding was not carried into #329, which consolidated workflows with cancel-in-progress: true and was flagged for the same class of hazard (#329/F8).

evidence: The PR deleted release.yml, yet the new comment said 'release.yml looks it up by the tag's target commit'. 62afcbe rewords it to 'the publish job below downloads it by the same SHA within this run'.
guidance_note: After deleting a file, grep the whole tree for its name, including the files you are editing, before pushing.

evidence: 'release.yml publishes it verbatim' refers to the deleted workflow. 62afcbe changes it to 'the publish job publishes it verbatim'.
guidance_note: After deleting a file, grep the whole tree for its name before pushing.

evidence: The original `grep -oE '^## \[[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\]' ... || true` returns empty for `## [0.2.0` and silently falls to release=false. 62afcbe splits out a malformed-heading error case.
guidance_note: When a resolver's empty result means 'no-op', enumerate the inputs that can produce empty (no match, malformed, missing file) and give each its own branch before writing `|| true`.

evidence: The agent admits its own sweep missed these: 'my grep missed these because the `release-validate.yml` filename prefix matched my own exclusion pattern (false NONE)'. 62afcbe removes the stale references.
guidance_note: When a stale-reference grep comes back empty, check the exclusion pattern did not also exclude the file being edited; search for the exact token `release.yml` with a word boundary.

evidence: '[LAW:single-enforcer] release.yml publishes using this IDENTICAL step' points at a deleted workflow. 62afcbe rewrites it to 'this workflow is the sole owner of the release build'.
guidance_note: After deleting a file, grep the whole tree for its name before pushing.

evidence: 'the IDENTICAL `release --clean` invocation release.yml used to run' compares against a workflow that no longer exists. 62afcbe rewords it without the reference.
guidance_note: After deleting a file, grep the whole tree for its name before pushing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the `path: dist` download is in the original publish job (shown in the round-1 hunk), and 62afcbe touched only comments and the kind resolver. The premise depends on upload-artifact@v4 keeping a `dist/` prefix. Its documented least-common-ancestor rule strips the prefix when every uploaded path is under dist/, which would make the reviewer's `path: .` the bug, but the packet does not show the full upload path list. The agent's nesting-agnostic `find metadata.json` locate is correct either way.
guidance_note: Before calling a third-party action's behaviour unverifiable, read its README; upload-artifact documents its least-common-ancestor stripping, and that settles whether the download path nests.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the consolidation in the original commit kept validate's `cancel-in-progress: true`, and 62afcbe did not touch the concurrency block. The reviewer is right that the deleted release.yml had cancel-in-progress false, so a second push could cancel an in-flight release. a4b97d8 sets it to false.
guidance_note: When merging two workflows into one, diff their top-level settings (concurrency, permissions, triggers) and carry over the stricter one for the path that publishes.

evidence: F3 was explicitly about `|| true` conflating distinct cases. 62afcbe's rewrite (`CAND=$(grep -E '^## \[' CHANGELOG.md | ... || true)`) separated malformed headings but still let a missing CHANGELOG (grep exit 2 under pipefail) collapse into 'no releases'. a4b97d8 adds `test -f`.
guidance_note: When fixing a `|| true` that conflates outcomes, list every exit code of every command in the pipeline (grep 0/1/2) and make sure only the benign one reaches the swallow.

evidence: This duplicates F7 (same line, same double-nesting claim), and the download step predates 62afcbe, so the flag is a false positive. Whether nesting occurs depends on upload-artifact's least-common-ancestor stripping, which the packet's partial upload paths do not settle. The find-based locate plus the non-empty asset assertion in a4b97d8 is correct under both layouts.

The flag is a false positive: the bare `gh release create` and its 'Re-runs are safe' comment were in the original publish job, untouched by 62afcbe. Whether gh can leave a tag without a release depends on gh's draft-then-publish behaviour when assets are passed, which the packet does not show. The agent took the reviewer's second option, a documented recovery path, and emits it on failure.

The flag is a false positive: `if git ls-remote --exit-code ... >/dev/null 2>&1` was in the original resolver, and 62afcbe only re-indented it under the new else branch. With --exit-code, 2 means no ref and 128 means a fatal error, so the `if` read an unreachable origin as 'release pending'. a4b97d8 branches on 0, 2 and anything else.
guidance_note: Before wrapping a command in `if`, check whether its exit status is boolean or multi-valued; for `git ls-remote --exit-code`, branch on 0 and 2 explicitly and fail on the rest.

evidence: The reviewer itself concludes 'Not a bug — confirming by design'. The local `git tag` lives only in the ephemeral runner checkout, and the real tag is created by `gh release create`. The flag is a false positive: the build-step tag predates a4b97d8.

narrative: This PR consolidated release.yml into release-validate.yml. Round 0 was mostly stale references to the deleted file that the agent's own grep had excluded, plus a silent fall-through in the version resolver. Round 1 landed on the fix commit but mostly flagged pre-existing publish-job issues: download nesting, the dropped cancel-in-progress false, the gh partial failure, and the ls-remote exit codes. Only the missing-CHANGELOG `|| true` gap was a remainder of the F3 fix. Round 2 raised only a self-dismissed non-issue.
guidance_observations: Most round-1 findings were pre-existing defects in the new publish job that one self-review pass of the silent-failure surface (exit codes, `|| true`, cancellation) would have caught before the first review.
The cancel-in-progress hazard had already been raised on the superseded #328 and was not carried forward.

evidence: detectVersionReuse compared only `f.sha256 != pin.sha256`, so `pin.file` was a stored copy nothing enforced. The agent took the reviewer's 'validate the filename' option as a new kindRenamed, which keeps the name kindDeleted needs while making it enforced.
guidance_note: Every field in a pinned identity struct needs a comparison in the detector; if a field is stored but never checked, either check it or delete it before review.

evidence: TestEveryReuseKindHasMessage fed a two-entry onDisk to kindDeleted, where the real detector produces nil, so an over-indexing explain() would pass the test and panic in production. 613a0c5 uses per-kind fixtures.
guidance_note: Build formatter test fixtures from the producer's documented per-kind shape, not one shared sample.

narrative: This PR adds a migration content-pinning gate. Both round-0 findings were real and fixed cleanly in one commit: the filename pin became enforced, and the test fixtures were shaped per kind. Round 1 was clean.

evidence: `bin=$(mktemp)` had no cleanup. The cost is trivial on ephemeral runners, and the `trap 'rm -f "$bin"' EXIT` added in 79351d6 is a one-line fix.

A supply-chain workflow curl'd and executed cyclonedx-cli with no integrity check. 79351d6 pins CYCLONEDX_CLI_SHA256 and runs `sha256sum -c -` before chmod. The agent's claim that no sidecar exists is unverifiable from the packet, but a pinned hash is the stronger choice either way.
guidance_note: In a workflow that downloads and executes a binary, pin its sha256 in the same edit that pins its version.

evidence: The reviewer's 'produces `"version": ""`' claim is wrong, because cyclonedx.Component.Version is `omitempty`. The test TestWriteSBOMOmitsEmptyAppVersion added in 79351d6 decodes to a map and asserts the key is absent. The untested-path half was right, so declining the guard while adding the test is the correct split.
guidance_note: When a CLI flag documents a behaviour for an empty value, add a test for that empty value in the original PR.

evidence: The flag is mostly a false positive: the ungated cyclonedx-cli download on every push was in the original commit, and 79351d6 only added the hash pin, which adds a hash-mismatch failure to that existing external dependency. Gating staging and validation on `steps.kind.outputs.release == 'true'` mirrors the existing upload gate.
guidance_note: When adding a step to a workflow that runs both release and snapshot builds, decide its gate explicitly by asking whether it prepares a publishable asset.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: TestRunHappyPath's switch to always passing sbomPath is in the original commit (the hunk shows the run() signature change), and 79351d6 touched sbom_test.go and the workflow, not main_test.go. The sbomPath="" success branch was indeed unreached, and 4c875fa adds TestRunWithoutSBOM.
guidance_note: When you change a function signature and update its happy-path test to the new mode, keep one test on the old mode too, since it is still a supported invocation.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: snapshot staging, which named the file from metadata.json's snapshot version while the content omitted the version, predates 79351d6. Release-gating staging in 4c875fa removes the snapshot case entirely, which is cleaner than threading the snapshot version in.

4c875fa's TestRunWithoutSBOM asserts the exact two-artifact summary, but the sibling TestRunHappyPath kept `strings.Contains(stdout.String(), "wrote")`. The reviewer points to that asymmetry explicitly, and f2d969a tightens it.
guidance_note: When adding a precise assertion to one test of a pair, upgrade the sibling's matching assertion in the same commit.

evidence: F6 was the filename-vs-content version mismatch. 4c875fa removed the snapshot instance by gating and added a comment asserting release-path agreement 'by construction', but nothing checks it. f2d969a adds the jq comparison. No release-path bug existed; the point is that the asserted invariant is now checked.
guidance_note: When a fix comment says two independently derived values agree 'by construction', add the one-line assertion in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: buildEntriesForPkg in sbom_test.go is original-PR code, and f2d969a touched only the workflow staging step and TestRunHappyPath. The duplication of run()'s classification pipeline was real, and 85f6c9c extracts buildEntries(pkg) for both callers.
guidance_note: When a test needs the production pipeline's output, extract the production function rather than copying its body into a test helper.

narrative: This PR adds a CycloneDX SBOM to the release. Rounds 0 and 1 found real but mostly pre-existing gaps: temp cleanup, the unverified binary download, the empty-version test, snapshot gating, and the orphaned no-SBOM path. Round 2's two findings were both remainders of round-1 fixes: the sibling test's assertion was left loose, and the 'by construction' version agreement was left unchecked. Their fixes forced round 3, which surfaced only a pre-existing duplicated test helper.
guidance_observations: Several flagged findings were on original-PR lines, which suggests one pre-review pass over test fidelity (fixture shape, assertion strength, duplicated pipelines) would have removed two rounds.
The agent's fixes were well-judged; the avoidable round came from fixing one instance without checking its sibling.

evidence: policy.json hardcodes 'Unknown', duplicating classify.go's `unclassifiedLicense`. 04d7cc8 adds TestBuzhashExceptionUsesClassifierSentinel, the reviewer's test option, which turns silent drift into a named test failure.
guidance_note: When a data file keys on a code constant's value, add the coupling test in the same PR that introduces the data file.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 04d7cc8 touched only policy.json and policy_test.go, not CHANGELOG.md. The reviewer's premise is conditional ('if it shipped with 0.2.1'), and 'the test predates this PR' does not show it shipped in 0.2.1. The agent cites `git merge-base --is-ancestor` returning false for b56b225 against v0.2.1, which the packet cannot confirm.

The flag is a false positive: the separate `go run ./tools/licenses -check` step is original-PR code, untouched by 04d7cc8. The drift is theoretical because the module inventory is pinned by go.sum. Removing the redundant step, which ci.yml's go test already covers on master pushes, and leaving the publish gate to sibling w6m9.5 was proportionate.

narrative: This PR adds the license-policy gate. Round 0 found a duplicated sentinel, fixed with a coupling test. Round 1's two findings sat on the fix commit but concerned untouched lines: a CHANGELOG placement claim the agent rebutted with git ancestry, and a redundant second inventory build the agent removed. Round 2 was clean.

evidence: The SBOM assertion slice covered icu, zstd and musl but not compiler-rt, the fourth entry in nativeLibs. e6b0ea3 adds it.
guidance_note: When adding N items to an inventory, drive every per-item assertion from the same list (or check each assertion has all N) rather than hand-listing a subset.

evidence: `strings.Contains(..., "MIT license")` is case-sensitive: it matches musl's 'standard MIT license' but not compiler-rt's 'The MIT License (Expat)', so compiler-rt's notice was never verified. e6b0ea3 pairs each library with a unique substring.
guidance_note: When one substring assertion is meant to cover several items, pair each item with its own unique substring so a missing item cannot hide behind another's match.

evidence: The release-archive grep checked musl and icu only, out of four native libraries. e6b0ea3 adds the zstd and compiler-rt report rows and notice text.
guidance_note: Same move as F1: an end-to-end check over a new inventory should cover every member, not a sample.

evidence: This PR appends nativeEntries() to buildEntries, so the SBOM now includes C libraries, but the existing Unreleased SBOM line still said 'every Go module'. e6b0ea3 rewords it.
guidance_note: When a change widens an artifact's scope, grep CHANGELOG and docs for existing descriptions of that artifact and update them in the same PR.

narrative: This PR adds native C libraries to the SBOM, bundle, report and policy. All four round-0 findings were real incompleteness in the original PR: three checks covered a subset of the four libraries, and the CHANGELOG went stale. All were fixed in one commit, and round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: Three of the four findings are the same move: assertions hand-listed a subset of a new four-item inventory.

evidence: The workflow test pinned only `nodeContains(publish.Needs, "license-gate")`, so dropping validate from needs would let publish race the build. 5c32c70 adds the validate assertion.
guidance_note: When a test pins a list-valued dependency you just extended, assert the whole required set, not only the member you added.

narrative: This PR adds a publish-blocking license-gate job. Round 0 found the structural test pinned only the new needs edge. The fix added the validate edge, and round 1 was clean.

evidence: The reviewer flagged a risk ('not verifiable from within this repo'). The agent answered it by citing action.yml at v1 (commit 7f7b67a), which declares DEPENDENCY_DIFF with default false; the packet cannot confirm that. Declining the SHA pin because the moving v1 tag is the installer's deliberate single source is a reasoned tradeoff, not a dodge.

narrative: This is a nine-line docs comment PR. The single advisory asked whether the external action accepts the input. The agent answered by checking the action's action.yml at the tag and declined the SHA-pin suggestion with a design reason.

evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md listed 'feature, fix, docs, or chore' while RELEASING.md also listed refactor. Rather than adding refactor, 8aa488f removed the enumeration from both ('No ticket PR, whatever its type'), which removes the drift instead of patching it.
guidance_note: When the same set is written out in two docs, state the rule without listing members, so neither list can go incomplete.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 8aa488f touched only CONTRIBUTING.md and RELEASING.md, and the duplicated CLAUDE.md procedure is original-PR text. The duplication was real, but keeping the one-sentence agent guardrail inline is justified for an always-loaded file. 6f2b760 replaces only the procedure with a pointer.
guidance_note: When writing a procedure that already lives in an operator's guide, write only the audience-specific rule plus a pointer in the other docs from the start.

evidence: 6f2b760 pointed CLAUDE.md at CONTRIBUTING.md as 'the authoritative procedure' while RELEASING.md still carried the same steps and policy. The F2 fix deduplicated one copy but picked a home that was itself one of two duplicates. The follow-up consolidated to RELEASING.md and repointed CLAUDE.md.
guidance_note: When a fix deduplicates by pointing at a canonical home, first confirm that home is the only remaining copy; with three copies, collapse to one in a single commit.

narrative: This docs PR moves releases to one per epic. Each round removed one duplicate: the type enumeration, then CLAUDE.md's procedure, then the CONTRIBUTING and RELEASING copy. Round 3 happened only because the round-1 fix pointed CLAUDE.md at CONTRIBUTING.md without noticing RELEASING.md also held the procedure.
guidance_observations: The procedure existed in three files at PR open; collapsing it to one home in the original PR would have removed all three findings.

evidence: The `retIdx <= opsIdx` comparison does track render order, since cobra renders groups in registration order, so the test was not purely structural. Asserting on `root.UsageString()` in d72338a checks the observable --help grouping directly and subsumes the membership checks.
guidance_note: When the acceptance criterion is how --help looks, assert on the rendered help from the start.

narrative: This PR splits transition verbs into help groups and retires `update --status`. The single advisory asked the grouping test to assert on rendered help instead of slice indices. The agent rewrote it, and round 1 was clean.
